title.narrative: Transforming food systems through ecosystem-based approaches to combat land degradation and loss in ecosystem services in value-chains in Tonga

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project will ensure that project staff adhere to both national employment and labour laws, as well as international commitments, and will increase the protection and promotion of worker health and safety. Sustainable agriculture, CSA, and regenerative farming practices including multi-crop systems and value-added processing, can create more jobs and income opportunities, especially in rural areas. Sustainable food systems in Tonga offer significant socio-economic benefits by enhancing food security, creating employment opportunities, and improving livelihoods, particularly for those involved in agriculture. Tonga has a strong tradition of subsistence farming, and prioritizing sustainable practices will strengthen this system, increase exports, and build resilience against climate change and economic shocks. Socio-economic benefits of the proposed project are highlighted below:Economic benefitsIncreased Exports: Tonga's agricultural sector is a major contributor to its economy, and sustainable practices can boost exports, particularly of crops like root crops (taro, yams, cassava) and watermelons. For example, the country aims to increase watermelon exports to New Zealand.Job Creation: Sustainable agriculture, including multi-crop systems and value-added processing, can create more jobs and income opportunities, especially in rural areas.Reduced Food Import Reliance: By strengthening local food production and promoting local food value chain, Tonga can decrease its reliance on imported food, which is often costly and subject to global price fluctuations.Strengthened Value Chains: Improving market infrastructure, promoting local food value chain, and processing can add value to agricultural products and improve their market access, both domestically and internationally.Social Benefits:Improved Food Security: Sustainable food systems ensure a more reliable and diverse supply of nutritious food, contributing to better health and well-being for the population.Community Resilience: Integrating traditional farming knowledge and community participation into sustainable practices can strengthen social structures and build resilience against climate change and economic shocks.Preservation of Biodiversity: Sustainable agriculture can help protect Tonga's valuable biodiversity, which is essential for ecosystem services like food production and cultural heritage.Empowerment of Women and Youth: Sustainable agriculture initiatives can create opportunities for women and young people to participate in the sector, contributing to their economic empowerment.Global reputation of Tongan Food System: Through the enabling environment at national scales, the project will promote sustainable rural livelihoods and employment, food security and nutrition, and facilitate restoration and resilience of agroecosystems. Public-private partnerships of this project will explore and develop market incentives and finance for CSA and regenerative practices that can deliver environmental livelihood and employment benefits. Investment in nature-based solutions under this project will improve water management, reduce pollution, and conserve key sources of natural- and agro-biodiversity. Integrated landscape management coupled encompassing on-farm technologies and nature-based solutions will enable farmers to sustainably increase productivity and generate environmental, livelihood, and rural employment benefits. Climate-smart, agroecological, and regenerative production practices at scale through improved extension services will increase the reputation of Tonga food systems. Global cooperation and knowledge exchange: Adaptive knowledge management and outreach at national and global levels via engagement with relevant platforms will further strengthen collaboration with other developing countries through South-South and Triangular Cooperation mechanisms and share its knowledge and experience in sustainable agriculture and food systems with other countries.Health and Safety: As indicated in Annex K: Gender analysis and action plan, the project will arrange special training for gender mainstreaming among project staff and community members (women and men). Hence, the project will ensure that the project staff adhere to both national employment and labour laws, as well as international commitments, and will increase the protection and promotion of worker health and safety. Capacity development of Women and Youth: Besides, the project has dedicated output under component 2 on capacity building of women and youth agri-entrepreneurs to engage in sustainable and resilient livelihoods. Under this component, there will be capacity building and piloting activities of alternative livelihoods development, which will focus on vulnerable group including women and youth.
To reverse land degradation and enhance the climate resilience of ecosystems and communities by applying integrated ecosystem-based approaches to food systems in Tonga.
